messages.content: 計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
在這個單樣本t檢定中，關鍵的是「抽樣分布的標準誤」（standard error, SE），它衡量樣本平均數與母體平均數之間的變異程度。  
公式如下：

\[
SE=\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}
\]

其中  
- \(s\)：樣本標準差（此處為 1.4）  
- \(n\)：樣本大小（此處為 40）

把數值代入：

\[
SE=\frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}}\approx \frac{1.4}{6.3249}\approx 0.2215
\]

所以，在以 \( \mu_0 = 98.6 \) 為零假設時，樣本平均數的抽樣分布（或稱「t 檢定的標準誤」）大約是 **0.22**。  

> **備註**：若你想進一步計算t統計量，只需將樣本平均數與零假設平均數之差除以上述標準誤即可。

The user says (in Chinese): "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" They want to calculate something about hypothesis testing? They mention sample mean 98.2, std dev 1.4, sample size 40, null hypothesis mean 98.6. They ask to compute the standard deviation? Actually they say "計算...的零假設檢定的標準差" which might mean compute the standard error or the standard deviation of the sampling distribution? They likely want to compute the standard error of the mean: sigma/sqrt(n). But we have sample standard deviation s=1.4, so SE = s / sqrt(n) = 1.4 / sqrt(40). Let's compute: sqrt(40)=6.3249; 1.4/6.3249=0.2215 approx.

But maybe they want to compute the standard deviation of the sampling distribution under null? That would be population standard deviation? But we don't know population SD. We can approximate using sample SD. So answer: 0.2215.

Alternatively, they might want to compute the standard deviation of the t-statistic? For t-test, t = (xbar - mu0)/(s/sqrt(n)). So denominator is SE. So standard deviation of t distribution is sqrt(df/(df-2))? Not needed.

Thus answer: 0.2215.
